tagline: Dive capital at the top of the Gulf triangle — single-pier dependency.
summary: Koh Tao is the northern vertex of the Samui Gulf triangle, ~30nm from Phangan and ~45nm from Samui. World-renowned dive tourism drives steady inbound flow funneled through a single main pier (Mae Haad), making reliable, weather-resilient transfers a real pain point.

demand_signals.detail: One of the world's busiest dive-certification destinations; steady visitor arrivals year-round.
Mae Haad concentrates nearly all arrivals — congestion and weather cancellations are chronic.

journeys.note: Longer hop, still in range; weather-gate in monsoon.

navier_fit: Medium-high. 30-45nm corridors sit inside Pioneer II range but need weather-gating; single-pier reliability is exactly where a premium, schedule-flexible service wins.
competitive_landscape: Lomprayah & Seatran catamarans from Chumphon/Phangan/Samui; cancellations common in rough Gulf swell.
seasonality: Peak: Dec-Apr. Strong monsoon Oct-Nov frequently closes the longer Tao crossings — range/weather gating essential.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage + Marine Department passenger licensing. Dive-operator partnerships likely the practical channel.

grab.super_app_fit: Grab booking for dive-school packaged transfers; reliability SLA as the differentiator vs cancellation-prone ferries.
grab.wedge: Weather-resilient premium crossing to a single-pier island where cancellations strand travelers — a clear reliability story.

transit_planning.note: Single-pier island; resilience is the value.

_enrichment.note: Connected city brief hung off the Koh Samui / Gulf flagship. Geometry sealed via Grok from Bucket-C BP files.
